oil.summary: Crude sold off sharply on Tuesday, with Brent tumbling 8.42% to $96.42 and WTI down 2.95% to $89.89, as a confluence of supply-side relief valves punctured the recent rally. Renewed Iran diplomatic talks and Trump's assertion the conflict will end 'very soon,' combined with recovering Hormuz flows and Saudi Arabia restarting Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu following the East-West pipeline partial resumption, all weighed on risk premia. A 40-million-barrel SPR release by the DoE added further downward pressure. Refined products were hit harder: RBOB fell 5.90% and heating oil dropped 4.70%, though diesel above $6 underscores lingering tightness. Geopolitical tail risks persist—Ukraine has struck 45% of Russian refining capacity, and the Graham Act's proposed 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian energy keeps India's crude sourcing calculus in focus. Options markets now price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting.
drivers: Iran diplomatic progress and recovering Strait of Hormuz flows deflate geopolitical risk premium, triggering broad crude sell-off
Saudi Arabia resumes Yanbu Red Sea loadings and U.S. releases 40 million barrels from the SPR, boosting near-term supply expectations
Ukraine strikes on Russian refining capacity and threatened 100% U.S. tariffs on Russian energy buyers keep medium-term supply risk elevated

gas.summary: The gas complex diverged sharply by geography today. TTF collapsed 7.22% to €68.135/MWh, likely tracking crude's risk-off move and partial easing of Hormuz-related LNG supply fears as Iran talks advanced. Henry Hub was a relative outperformer, adding 0.33% to $3.01/MMBtu, continuing a modest month-long grind higher of 4.22%. On the supply side, Shell approved Phase 2 of LNG Canada, doubling export capacity into the early 2030s—a longer-dated bearish signal for Atlantic Basin balances. China's LNG imports are headed for a second consecutive monthly decline, attributed to elevated war-driven prices, softening a key demand pillar. Europe's LNG buying spree continues under a ticking clock, while the EU is reportedly weighing a one-year delay to methane import reporting rules as winter supply risks clash with regulatory ambition.
drivers: TTF drops sharply as Iran talks reduce immediate Hormuz LNG disruption fears, while Henry Hub holds firm on domestic demand dynamics
Shell approves LNG Canada Phase 2, doubling export capacity by the early 2030s and adding future Atlantic Basin supply
China's LNG imports set for a second monthly decline amid high prices; EU considers delaying methane rules as winter supply anxiety mounts

power.summary: The power and carbon complex was relatively quiet on headline flow today, with EU EUAs slipping 1.24% to $81.60—a modest pullback within a still-positive monthly trend of +4.41%. The move broadly mirrors the softening in TTF, which fell 7.22% and typically provides a directional guide for carbon as gas-to-coal switching incentives shift. On the policy front, Spain, Portugal, and Luxembourg jointly called for the EU to establish a binding 2040 renewable energy target, a medium-term bullish signal for carbon floor prices. The World Bank injected fresh funding into Tajikistan's Rogun Dam, the world's tallest dam project, signalling incremental growth in zero-carbon hydro capacity in Central Asia. Headline flow for this sector was relatively thin today beyond these items.
drivers: EUA prices dip modestly, tracking TTF lower as gas risk premium eases following Iran diplomatic developments
Spain, Portugal, and Luxembourg push for an EU 2040 renewable energy target, reinforcing longer-term structural demand for carbon allowances
World Bank renews funding for Tajikistan's Rogun Dam, adding to the pipeline of large-scale zero-carbon hydro capacity
